title: Additional Protocols I and II to the Geneva Conventions
summary: On 8 June 1977 a diplomatic conference in Geneva adopted two Protocols supplementing the 1949 Geneva Conventions: Protocol I on international armed conflicts and Protocol II on non-international ones. They added rules on protecting civilians and on civil wars, and entered into force on 7 December 1978.

uncertainty.note: Start is the adoption date; end is entry into force.

as_recorded.value: June 8, 2017 marks the 40 th anniversary of the adoption of the two Protocols

importance.justification: Extended the laws of war to the conduct of hostilities, civilian protection and civil wars, and are now binding on well over 160 states.

related.because: Gaps in the 1949 texts on the conduct of hostilities and on internal conflicts led states to negotiate supplementary protocols.

beats.caption: A diplomatic conference in Geneva adopted Protocols I and II, supplementing the four 1949 Geneva Conventions.
Both Protocols entered into force, with rules on conduct of hostilities and on civil wars.
By October 2020, 174 states were party to Protocol I and 169 to Protocol II, extending civilian protection in war.
